I would definitely rent before buying if possible to try out different guns. You want to identify the general category of trigger function you like best:

”Safe Action”: The Glock style which uses a striker with no exposed hammer and the same medium weight trigger pull every time. Consistent and simple operation, but people complain the triggers are “mushy”.

Single Action Only: The type of operation on a 1911. The hammer needs to be manually cocked for the first shot. The trigger pull is consistently lighter and generally crisper since all it does is drop the hammer.

Double Action: The trigger pull is consistently heavy since the trigger pull will both cock the hammer and drop it. This is common on a lot of revolvers.

Double Action/Single Action: This is something like a Berretta 92. The first shot is a heavy double action that cocks the trigger, all follow up shots are in single action mode. Takes some getting used to.

Then decide if you want or don’t want a manual safety.
